content: Figure FIGREF20 shows the counts of group labels for each year in the New York Times from 1986 to 2015. For visualization purposes, only words with a total count greater than 1000 are shown. Notably, the relative frequency of homosexual decreased substantially over time, while gay, lesbian, and bisexual are more frequent in later years. We also see the emergence of the terms lgbt and transgender after 2000. Aggregated counts over all years for each LGBTQ label can be found in the Appendix.
